summary: Fix the three failing CI lanes on 49c08aa: Core shutdown now waits for a background update apply (and the update check no longer reports done over a running apply), release asset uploads retry a dropped connection and refuse a short upload, and Controller startup waits in the integration harness allow for a loaded runner and print the process log when they give up. Two agent checks also asserted wall-clock numbers a busy runner controls. BUG-0274, BUG-0275, BUG-0276, BUG-0277.

guide.reason: Two operator-visible behaviours changed. Publishing a release now resends an asset the forge drops part-way through and fails a short upload instead of publishing it, with new messages an operator reads in the run; the release page records both, in the expected result and in troubleshooting. On Core, the Updates page keeps showing the real step while the same host is applying, and stopping Core during an apply waits for apt rather than interrupting it, so a stop that takes minutes is expected and not a fault. The existing stuck-phase recovery is unchanged and still documented.

api.reason: GET /api/local/v1/updates and POST /api/local/v1/updates/apply keep their request, response and status contract. The reported phase now follows the running apply instead of clearing to done when apt reports the new version mid-install, and stopping the service waits for an apply it started; docs/API.md states both in the software updates section. No field, status code, authorization or retry behaviour changes, so the generated references are unchanged.

roadmap.reason: No milestone status changes; this fixes CI lanes and update shutdown behaviour inside the already published 0.3.2 scope.

state.reason: No new or changed durable record. The host-side update progress file the apply writes already exists and keeps its format and location; the fix only stops a writer outliving the shutdown that owns its directory.

verification.method: go test -race ./internal/localcore ./internal/nexupdate passed. TestCloseWaitsForTheBackgroundUpdate fails with the wait removed ('Close returned while the apply was still writing to the state directory', race detected) and passes with it; TestMergeProgressLeavesARunningApplyAlone reports done with the guard removed. python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_gitea_release.py' passed 6 tests; the dropped-upload test fails with UPLOAD_ATTEMPTS = 1. Controller startup measured at 0.10s from a fresh data directory, and Lab.started() was exercised by hand on a healthy start and on a Controller missing its source archive, which printed its log. Failing CI evidence read from the forge: run 4064 (release asset upload), run 4063 go lane (TempDir cleanup), run 4067 controller-browser (gallery startup). internal/agent timing checks passed -count=4 with all 16 cores saturated. Full go test -race ./... passed except internal/vmhost TestRegisterDefaultsIsIdempotentAndRespectsExistingEntries, which needs root for runuser locally and is green in CI. 310 tests/test_*.py ran: only test_website_hosting failed, needing nginx, which CI installs. python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree, scripts/generate_api.py --check and the repository privacy test passed. Guide walkthrough: the documented Core behaviour is the behaviour the new checks assert (TestCloseWaitsForTheBackgroundUpdate for the waiting stop, TestMergeProgressLeavesARunningApplyAlone for the reported step); the release-page text matches the implemented retry and size check in scripts/gitea-release.py and its tests, but no release run has been published since, so the forge-side walkthrough is outstanding and the next release run is that evidence.
